info.title: How does &snapper; clean up old snapshots?

topic.para: &snapper; deletes old snapshots automatically to prevent the root partition from running out of space. The cleanup algorithms differentiate between timeline snapshots and numbered snapshots (pre and post snapshot pairs created by package installations).

section.title: Cleanup criteria
section.para: You can configure the cleanup behavior based on the following criteria:

listitem.para: Number limit: The system can be set to automatically delete old snapshots when a certain count of snapshots is reached.
Age limit: Old snapshots can be deleted if they exceed a certain age, while still preserving a number of snapshots for each time period (hourly, daily, monthly, yearly).
Pre and post snapshot pairs: pre and post snapshot pairs that do not differ can be automatically deleted.

section.title: Cleanup parameters and defaults
section.para: The following parameters control the cleanup. The default values apply to the root partition.

listitem.para: For numbered snapshots, the cleanup is controlled by parameters such as NUMBER_CLEANUP, NUMBER_LIMIT, NUMBER_LIMIT_IMPORTANT, and NUMBER_MIN_AGE. The default values for the root partition are 2-10 for NUMBER_LIMIT and 4-10 for NUMBER_LIMIT_IMPORTANT. This means that &snapper; keeps up to ten of the youngest snapshots of each kind, and reduces their number to the lower value if the root partition is running out of space.

Timeline snapshots are disabled for the root partition by default (TIMELINE_CREATE="no"). If you enable them, the cleanup is based on the number of snapshots to keep for each interval. With the default values, &snapper; keeps the last ten hourly snapshots and the first snapshot of each of the last ten days, months and years. The parameters include TIMELINE_CLEANUP, TIMELINE_MIN_AGE and interval parameters such as TIMELINE_LIMIT_HOURLY, TIMELINE_LIMIT_DAILY and so on.
